Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans | A: Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans | AX1S Infra
Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans: wa: Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans: which fits your workload?
Twee wegen naar dezelfde korting: Two routes to the same discount
Zodra een workload voorspelbaar en conti: As soon as a workload runs predictably and continuously, you leave money on the table by paying everything at the on-demand rate. Cloud providers reward commitment with substantial discounts, generally between 20 and 60 percent, depending on term and type of commitment. The two best-known routes are Reserved Instances (RIs) and Savings Plans. They look alike, but the differences determine in practice how much flexibility you retain.
Reserved Instances: maximale korting, mi: Reserved Instances: maximum discount, less flexibility
Met een Reserved Instance commit je aan: With a Reserved Instance you commit to a specific instance type, in a specific region, for a period of usually one or three years. The discount is generally the highest, especially with an upfront payment. The flip side: if your architecture changes, or you switch to a different instance type, the reservation no longer matches and you still miss out on the return.
Savings Plans: iets minder korting, veel: Savings Plans: slightly lower discount, much more room to move
Een Savings Plan werkt anders: je commit: A Savings Plan works differently: you commit to a fixed amount of usage per hour, regardless of which instance type, family or even (with some providers) region you use. That makes the instrument resilient to architectural changes. The discount is generally slightly lower than with an RI of the same term, but the risk of "wasted" commitment is considerably smaller.
{1} Stabiele, langdurig ongewijzigde wor: {1} Stable, long-unchanged workload on a fixed instance type? A Reserved Instance delivers the highest discount.
{1} Groeiende of veranderende infrastruc: {1} Growing or changing infrastructure, migrations planned, or multiple teams making their own instance choices? Go for a Savings Plan.
{1} Twijfel je? Begin met een Savings Pl: {1} In doubt? Start with a Savings Plan on your most predictable base usage and build it out gradually.
De grootste fout die we zien is niet het: The biggest mistake we see is not choosing the wrong instrument, but committing to too much volume. Always calculate on the basis of your minimum, structural usage over recent months, not on your peak load. Anything above that you simply leave running on on-demand.
Vuistregel: committeer nooit op meer dan: Rule of thumb: never commit to more than 70 to 80 percent of your average usage. That way you keep room for seasonal fluctuations and growth, without missing the discount on your base usage.
Combineren kan, en is vaak optimaal: Combining is possible, and often optimal
In de praktijk werkt een gelaagde aanpak: In practice a layered approach works best: Savings Plans for the flexible base, supplemented with targeted Reserved Instances on the workloads that demonstrably stay stable for years. That does require ongoing monitoring: commitments are not a one-off decision, but an instrument you need to recalibrate periodically as your infrastructure changes.

Dit zijn de vragen die we het vaakst kri: These are the questions we get most often about cloud costs and FinOps, gathered in one place. No jargon contest, just direct answers. For the underlying terms you can also consult the {1}FinOps Glossary{/1}.
Waarom cloudkosten uit de hand lopen: Why cloud costs get out of hand
Waarom stijgen onze cloudkosten sneller: Why are our cloud costs rising faster than our revenue?
Cloudinfrastructuur schaalt mee met gebr: Cloud infrastructure scales with usage, but without active steering it also scales with carelessness: new features run on new resources, old resources are rarely cleaned up, and nobody feels the bill directly. Revenue growth and technology growth therefore often drift apart until someone explicitly steers on it.
Hoeveel van een gemiddeld cloudbudget is: How much of an average cloud budget is waste?
Dat verschilt sterk per organisatie, maa: That differs greatly per organisation, but unused cloud capacity often quickly eats up 10 to 15 percent of the cloud budget as soon as nobody structurally tracks usage.
Wat zijn signalen dat een organisatie ge: What are signs that an organisation has no grip on cloud costs?
Niemand kan in één zin uitleggen waar he: Nobody can explain in one sentence what the cloud budget is spent on, the invoice is opened with surprise afterwards instead of being predicted beforehand, and nobody is explicitly responsible for the costs, only for the technology behind them.
Cloudkosten besparen: de praktische kant: Saving on cloud costs: the practical side
Wat is rightsizing en hoeveel levert het: What is rightsizing and how much does it deliver?
Rightsizing is het aanpassen van de capa: Rightsizing is adjusting the capacity of a resource to actual usage. Instances are often chosen too generously at the start of a project and never reconsidered afterwards. Based on usage data, 20 to 40 percent savings can usually be achieved on the workload concerned, without any impact on performance.
Wat is het verschil tussen Reserved Inst: What is the difference between Reserved Instances and Savings Plans?
Beide zijn commitment-kortingen in ruil: Both are commitment discounts in exchange for a usage or spend commitment. A Reserved Instance is tied to a specific instance type and region, a Savings Plan commits to a fixed amount of compute spend per hour, regardless of which instance type you use. Savings Plans are more flexible, Reserved Instances sometimes give a slightly higher discount for highly predictable workloads. (The full comparison is in {1}Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans{/1}.)
Hoe krijg je cloudkosten inzichtelijk pe: How do you make cloud costs visible per team or customer?
Via cost allocation: consistente tagging: Through cost allocation: consistent tagging on team, project and environment, followed by chargeback or showback so teams see for themselves what their infrastructure costs. Once that is visible, behaviour often changes by itself.
Hoe zit het met de kosten van AI en LLM': What about the costs of AI and LLMs within FinOps?
AI-kostenbeheer is een eigen aandachtsge: AI cost management has become a focus area of its own within FinOps: compute for training and inference, API costs from model providers and data storage quickly add up and are often not yet separately visible in existing cost reports. The same discipline (measure, allocate, optimise) applies, only the tooling and the recognition of waste are still less mature than with traditional cloud compute.
Kort samengevat: teams krijgen zelf zich: In short: teams gain visibility into their own cloud and AI usage and take responsibility for it, instead of finance checking it afterwards. That cross-functional interplay between finance, engineering and operations is the core of FinOps. (See also {1}What is FinOps?{/1} for the full explanation.)
De FinOps Lifecycle bestaat uit drie doo: The FinOps Lifecycle consists of three continuous phases: Inform (visibility and cost allocation), Optimize (rightsizing, commitments and eliminating waste) and Operate (embedding in processes and team behaviour). The phases are repeated, not gone through once.
Wie is binnen een organisatie verantwoor: Who within an organisation is responsible for cloud costs?
In de praktijk niemand, tenzij het expli: In practice nobody, unless it is explicitly assigned. Engineering mainly optimises for performance and speed, finance sees the bill but often lacks technical context. FinOps is meant to make those two worlds speak the same language, with a clear owner for costs per team.
Is FinOps alleen relevant voor grote bed: Is FinOps only relevant for large companies?
Nee. Scale-ups en SaaS-bedrijven merken: No. Scale-ups and SaaS companies feel the impact of unmanaged cloud costs sooner, because infrastructure costs have a more direct effect on margin and cash runway. The sooner the basics are in place (visibility, tagging, ownership), the less needs cleaning up later.

Beide kan. Veel organisaties starten zel: Both are possible. Verspilling in de cloud is zelden het ge: Waste in the cloud is rarely the result of one big mistake. It builds up from small choices that seemed logical at the time.
Deze drie stappen brengen dat systematis: These three steps map it out systematically, without you having to set up a full FinOps project right away.
1. Vergelijk toegewezen capaciteit met d: 1. Compare allocated capacity with actual usage
De meeste verspilling zit niet in wat er: Most waste isn't in what is running, but in what has been set up needlessly large. Servers, storage and databases are often configured more generously than needed, "to be safe," and then stay unchanged for years. Put allocated capacity next to actual usage over the past 30 days. Anything with structurally low utilisation is a first candidate to downsize or switch off.
2. Zoek naar resources zonder eigenaar: 2. Look for resources without an owner
Elke cloudomgeving verzamelt na verloop: Over time every cloud environment collects resources that were once created for a specific project, which has since been completed or stopped. The resource itself happily keeps running, and nobody feels responsible for it any more. Search the environment by tags, labels and creation date. Anything without a clear owner or an actively linked project deserves a conversation: still needed, or simply never switched off. At AX1S this comes up in almost every scan, often accounting for a considerable part of the first savings found. With the {1}FinOps Radar{/1} you get a first indication within 2 minutes of how much of this there could be at your organisation.
3. Controleer of contracten nog aansluit: 3. Check whether contracts still match current usage
Reserved instances en savings plans zijn: Reserved instances and savings plans were once taken out based on an expected usage pattern. If that pattern has changed, for example through a migration or an architecture change, the contract often stays in place while no longer being optimal. Compare current commitments with actual usage via the {1}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/1}. A contract that was once advantageous may by now be costing money instead of saving it.

5 stappen naar een voorspelbaar cloudbud: 5 steps to a predictable cloud budget | AX1S Infra
De meeste cloudbudgetten zijn geen budge: Most cloud budgets aren't a budget. It's last year, plus a margin. By the end of the quarter it turns out nobody can explain exactly why it turned out differently. Not because something went wrong, but because there was never a structure in place to predict it.
Deze vijf stappen zien we terugkomen bij: These five steps are what we see recurring at organisations that do get their cloud budget under control.
Veel bedrijven stellen eerst een bedrag: Many companies first set an amount and look for the justification afterwards. Rather, first look at what is actually running now, who uses it and why. At AX1S we find that this is the step that is skipped most often. Want a quick first indication without sitting down for it yourself? The {1}FinOps Radar{/1} gives a first picture of your savings potential within 2 minutes.
Normaal gebruik, groei en piekbelasting: Normal usage, growth and peak load produce three completely different amounts. Anyone who calculates with just one fixed number is almost guaranteed to be off. This is particularly relevant for AI workloads: a pilot with 50 users behaves completely differently financially from the same feature with 5,000 users. With the {1}AI Cost Calculator{/1} you can calculate that growth, including the breakdown and projection.
3. Leg vast wie waarvoor verantwoordelij: 3. Define who is responsible for what
Een voorspelbaar budget vraagt om duidel: A predictable budget requires clear ownership: who may decide on new capacity, new tools, or new AI integrations. Without that ownership a familiar pattern emerges: engineering builds, finance pays, and nobody has a real overview. At AX1S we see this in almost every intake conversation: the question "who decided on this?" more often gets a shrug than a name.
4. Zet automatische signalering in, niet: 4. Use automatic alerting, not monthly reports
Een rapportage aan het einde van de maan: A report at the end of the month comes too late; the money has already been spent. Set up interim alerting as soon as a team approaches a preset percentage of the budget, so you can adjust before it becomes an overrun.
5. Herzie het budget elk kwartaal, niet: 5. Review the budget every quarter, not every year
Cloud- en AI-omgevingen veranderen snell: Cloud and AI environments change faster than an annual budgeting cycle can keep up with. A budget set once a year is outdated again within a few months. Build in a fixed quarterly moment at which usage, scenarios and ownership are reviewed again. Still unsure whether your reserved instances or savings plans are the right starting point? The {1}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/1} compares on-demand, reserved instances and savings plans without you having to leave an email address.
Een voorspelbaar cloudbudget is geen kwe: A predictable cloud budget isn't a matter of guessing better, but of structure: usage as the starting point, scenarios instead of one number, clear ownership, interim alerting, and a fixed rhythm.
Kun je op dit moment zonder te zoeken ze: Can you right now, without looking, say what your cloud budget will do this quarter at 20% growth? If not, that is exactly where step 2 makes the difference.

Vier vragen die het eigenaarschap snel b: Four questions that quickly expose ownership
Bij de meeste organisaties bestaat er ge: At most organisations there is no doubt about who pays the invoices. There is, however, about who actually steers what is being spent.
These four questions expose that quickly. Ask them internally, and the answer (or the lack of one) immediately tells you where ownership is missing.
1. Wie mag beslissen om nieuwe cloud- of: 1. Who may decide to switch on new cloud or AI capacity?
Bij veel organisaties is het antwoord: i: At many organisations the answer is: anyone with the right access permissions. A developer can put a new instance or a new AI model live without a financial check in between. That is not a matter of carelessness. It was simply never defined who may make that decision, and who is responsible for the result afterwards.
2. Wie ziet een kostenstijging als eerst: 2. Who sees a cost increase first, and how quickly?
Bij de meeste bedrijven ligt het antwoor: At most companies the answer lies somewhere between "at the end of the month" and "if finance happens to notice." By then the money has already been spent, and adjusting is no longer possible, only explaining. Whoever steers sees a deviation within days, not at the end of a billing cycle.
3. Wie kan uitleggen waarom een kostenpo: 3. Who can explain why a cost item has risen, without first having to find out?
Bij AX1S vragen we dit vaak als eerste t: At AX1S we often ask this first during an intake: "why did this item rise last month?" The answer is rarely immediate. Usually a search through invoices and dashboards comes first before an explanation follows. That delay is itself the answer: if nobody knows right away, nobody is actively steering on it either.
4. Wie wordt aangesproken als het budget: 4. Who is held accountable when the budget is exceeded?
Niet wie ervoor opdraait op de balans, m: Not who bears it on the balance sheet, but who is in the conversation when it goes wrong. At many organisations that is nobody specific; the overrun is simply accepted as "just how it went." Without a point of accountability, cost management remains non-committal, however good the intentions.
Vier korte vragen, en meestal wordt al b: Four short questions, and usually it becomes clear from the first one what is wrong. Not because of ill will, but because steering was never explicitly assigned.
